claim: On 2024-09-24 Amazon S3 began applying a default to Lifecycle configurations that prevents objects smaller than 128 KB from being transitioned to any storage class. To let smaller objects transition, you add an object size filter to the transition rule with a custom minimum size (ObjectSizeGreaterThan) or maximum size (ObjectSizeLessThan).
question: What default did S3 Lifecycle add in September 2024 for small objects, and can you change it?

values.spoken: smaller than one hundred twenty-eight kilobytes

qualifiers.condition: override with an object size filter

evidence.quote: | [New default minimum object size transition behavior for Amazon S3 Lifecycle configurations](#WhatsNew) | Amazon S3 now applies a default behavior to S3 Lifecycle configurations that prevents objects smaller than 128 KB from being transitioned to any storage class. To learn how to override this behavior, see [Allowing objects smaller than 128 KB to be transitioned](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-configuration-examples.html#lc-small-objects). | September 24, 2024 |

To allow smaller objects to transition, you can add an [object size filter](intro-lifecycle-rules.md#intro-lifecycle-rules-filter) to your Lifecycle transition rules that specifies a custom minimum size (`ObjectSizeGreaterThan`) or maximum size (`ObjectSizeLessThan`).

note: d036. Old default (small objects could go only to Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive) is in s3-lifecycle-small-object-default.

claim: AWS positions S3 Files for data that is already in S3 and must be used by file-based applications, AI agents or teams with standard file operations; Amazon EFS for a fully managed shared file system as primary storage where data originates in and is mainly accessed through the file system; and Amazon FSx for existing applications that run on network-attached file storage.
question: When should you choose S3 Files, Amazon EFS or Amazon FSx?

values.display: you already have data in S3
values.spoken: S3 Files when the data already lives in S3
EFS as primary shared file storage

qualifiers.scope: choosing file access for AWS compute

evidence.quote: Use S3 Files when you already have data in S3 and you need file-based applications, AI agents, or teams to work with it directly using standard file operations.

Use Amazon EFS when you need a fully managed, cloud-native shared file system as your primary storage for workloads like shared home directories, content management, application configuration, and development environments where your data originates in and is primarily accessed through the file system.
Use Amazon FSx if you have existing file-based applications that run on network-attached file storage.

note: d007, d164. How AWS positions S3 Files against EFS; keep EFS as the default answer for a primary shared POSIX file system.
